commands.author: hugenshen

target.title: test(gateway): lock config mutation allowlist contract
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `gateway` built-in tool is a **persistent control-plane write surface**: agent-driven `config.apply` / `config.patch` can change live gateway config without operator CLI involvement. Per `SECURITY.md` and [Control plane tools risk](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security#control-plane-tools-risk), **the model/agent is not a trusted principal** — the runtime must fail closed and only permit a narrow, hand-maintained allowlist.

That allowlist lives in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts:54` as `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS`. On current `main` it is a **mutable string array with no contract lock**:

| Existing coverage | What it proves | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway-tool-guard-coverage.test.ts` (~43 behavioral cases) | Many real patches are allowed/blocked | Does **not** fail when someone adds/removes/reorders allowlist patterns |
| `gateway-tool.test.ts` | Tool schema exposes `replacePaths` | Does **not** exercise guard semantics with `replacePaths` |
| `src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts` | Gateway RPC rejects destructive array shrinks without `replacePaths` | Tests **server merge policy**, not the gateway-tool path allowlist after merge |

**Risk without this PR:** a maintainer can widen the agent-tunable surface (for example `plugins.allow`, `gateway.auth.token`, `tools.exec.host`) and existing guard tests may still pass if nobody adds a new behavioral case.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a **focused contract test** that complements (not replaces) `gateway-tool-guard-coverage.test.ts`:

1. **Snapshot lock** — exact sorted contents of `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS` (18 patterns today)
2. **Compact forbidden-path table** — representative high-impact paths that must stay blocked
3. **`replacePaths` guard boundary** — wholesale `agents.list` replacement must still respect the allowlist
4. **Real gateway-tool execution path** — `createGatewayTool().execute()` for `config.patch` / `config.apply`, with mocked `config.get` + RPC forwarding, so proof covers the same tool entrypoint models use

Minimal prod change: export a **frozen** allowlist snapshot for tests only (`ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS_FOR_TEST`). No runtime behavior change.

## User Impact

- **Runtime:** none
- **Operators:** none
- **Maintainers:** intentional allowlist changes require updating both:
  1. `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS` in `gateway-tool.ts`
  2. `LOCKED_ALLOWLIST` in `gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts`

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-gateway-allowlist-contract.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent-driven `gateway config.patch` / `config.apply` must fail closed on protected paths and accept only allowlisted mutations through the real gateway tool execution path.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-gateway-allowlist-contract.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-gateway-allowlist-contract.mjs
=== gateway allowlist contract proof (createGatewayTool config.patch/config.apply) ===

 ✓ createGatewayTool config.patch accepts allowlisted edits and forwards RPC
 ✓ createGatewayTool config.patch rejects protected edits before RPC
 ✓ createGatewayTool config.apply rejects protected replacements before RPC

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - `createGatewayTool().execute({ action: "config.patch", ... })` accepts an allowlisted `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` patch and forwards `config.patch` RPC with the resolved `baseHash`.
  - Protected `gateway.auth.token` patches are rejected with `gateway config.patch cannot change protected config paths: gateway.auth.token` **before** any `config.patch` RPC is sent.
  - Protected `config.apply` replacements are rejected with the same guard **before** any `config.apply` RPC is sent.
  - Contract tests also lock the frozen allowlist snapshot and `replacePaths` boundaries.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway RPC round-trip against a running gateway process; proof uses mocked `callGatewayTool` for `config.get` / write RPC forwarding while exercising the production `createGatewayTool` execute path and guard.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-gateway-allowlist-contract.mjs`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No runtime change; test seam now exports a frozen allowlist snapshot instead of the live mutable array reference
- Highest-risk area: accidental widening of the agent-tunable config surface during future allowlist edits
- Mitigation: sorted allowlist contract test fails CI on drift; forbidden-path and `replacePaths` cases stay blocked

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup
